question: How do I write down what a customer can rely on from our service so a fulfilment claim stays checkable later?
Our SLA doc mixes together what we guarantee, who is on the hook, and the tickets that delivered it — which pattern untangles that?
One diagram in our docs is being read as the procedure, the tool's ability, and the record of a run all at once. What helps me pull those apart?
Our team keeps treating an SOP document as if it were the capability to do the job — what helps separate the doc, the way of doing, and the ability?
A standard we cited got superseded — how do I figure out which of our existing decisions actually depended on the old claim?
Someone wants to add yet another core concept to our framework — how do we check that the existing kinds can't already express it?
Instead of a binary switch for whether something counts as an autonomous actor, is there a graded way to assess how much self-directed capacity a system has?
The board says a ticket is 'good to start' — how do I check we truly have everything in place before committing, without treating the green label as an approval?
Everything for the job looks lined up on paper, but nobody confirmed the inputs are actually on hand — where does FPF stop us from starting on hope?
We have several pass/fail signals feeding one go/no-go call — how should the worst signal drive whether the action may proceed?
One required verification came back unknown rather than pass — should the go/no-go call hold the action or let it through?
Two teams claim their terms mean the same thing across their glossaries — what discipline stops us hand-waving that the two senses match?
A bunch of coordinated parts now behaves like a regulated system with its own goals — when do we stop calling it the old thing and recognize something new?
When a commissioning project crosses into live operation, do we restart the assurance case for a newly identified whole or keep the old one?
A certification from decades ago still anchors our trust in this component — how does FPF treat proof that has gone stale?
How do I account for test results losing their weight over time when I aggregate assurance?
Our run-time system keeps drifting away from its design docs, and lessons learned never make it back into the spec — which pattern gives the cycle that closes that gap?
We hit a surprising anomaly and need a disciplined way to propose candidate explanations without locking onto the first plausible guess — where is that covered?
How strongly is a claim actually warranted by its linked evidence, and how does that strength travel along a justification path without being silently averaged?
Two pieces of evidence with different strength support one claim across a scope translation — how do I carry the warrant along the path without averaging?
I have a set of options in hand — when is it right to pick now versus paying for another probe or more computation first?
Is it worth gathering more information before committing to one of the choices on the table, given that probing costs something?
Several candidate research lines are still active — how do we decide whether to widen the frontier, keep it, narrow to a subset, or retire a line?
How do we keep several promising alternatives alive under one policy instead of prematurely collapsing to the single best scorer?
Terms like resilience or maintainability get squashed into a single score — how does FPF keep an -ility from being treated as one scalar?
Our org's team boundaries keep forcing every release into cross-team coordination, and the product structure mirrors it — which pattern handles deciding what to change on which side?
We want the service boundaries to stop mirroring the org chart — do we change the teams or the architecture first, and what counts as evidence either way?
A project's interests clash with the surrounding community's — how do I write down each side's claim and the tension between them before anyone tries to mediate?
Part of the system serves the whole while harming its own members — where do I lay out both sides' stakes at their different levels?
Can I mention CI/CD or file formats in a core normative pattern, or do tool-specific terms have to stay out?
When we amend several patterns together, where do we capture why the change was chosen and which alternatives were rejected, so reviewers don't have to dig through patch history?
Several sections must change together as one coordinated set — where do I record the shared decision so the pieces don't drift apart during the rewrite?
We're about to rework an existing spec section — how do I tell which downstream uses must be reopened and which can safely continue?
An agent is allowed to act without a human approving each step — how do we declare hard limits, an override path, and an audit trail for that leeway?
How do I set an explicit budget for what an unsupervised process may do on its own, with a standard way to pause or de-scope it?
A new role-ish word showed up in our docs — how do I decide whether it deserves a durable name or should stay a local phrase reusing an existing row?
We want to rename a long-standing term without breaking what older documents meant — what's the discipline for that?
Old documents still use the previous label for a concept we split in two — how do we keep readers able to connect past texts to the new senses?
We're surveying a fast-moving literature with rival schools that disagree on basics — how do we assemble a comparable, citable view without collapsing the plurality?
Multiple downstream consumers need to cite and replay the same chain of established results — what should we build so each doesn't redo the full source account?
